function: Joint learned control of uplink transmit power and PD-NOMA subcarriers, CPU cycles and UAV location, maximizing connections that meet the end-to-end delay limit (p. 8).
system: Uplink PD-NOMA, 30 IIoT nodes, 3 UAV aerial base stations plus HAPS relay, 8 subcarriers of 120 kHz, no RIS; antennas and carrier frequency not stated (p. 11).
method: Multi-agent recurrent deterministic policy gradient (MARDPG), actor-critic reinforcement learning with LSTM experience-sharing module and a critic over all agents' actions; trained 4500 episodes (p. 8-9, 11).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rayleigh fading with reference gain 1.4e-4 and Al-Hourani air-to-ground LoS-probability path loss; 30 nodes random in 2000x2000 m zone; no public dataset (p. 5-6, 11).
test_conditions: Trained 4500 episodes with U=30, B=3, K=8, DTh=100 ms (p. 11); evaluated in the same simulator while sweeping K, U, DTh and number of UAVs; no unseen scenario (p. 12).
baselines: Learned: MADDPG (fully connected networks) and distributed SAC; non-learned: Greedy policy and exhaustive search; min-delay objective variants run with MARDPG (p. 9, 12-13, 15).
metrics: Number of satisfactory connections (NSCs), episodic reward convergence, optimality gap to exhaustive search (6.67%), fairness score of user rates, run time, complexity and signaling overhead (p. 10-15).
complexity: Order O((E x Hbatch x HLSTM) x CCneural x B) and signaling overhead (Table 1, p. 10); MARDPG run time 12 ms versus 960 ms for exhaustive search (Table 4, p. 15).
openness: Source code released as IEEE DataPort dataset, DOI 10.21227/xsb6-ah82 (p. 12, 18).
q1_support: p. 5: "Rayleigh fading channel gain with the reference-distance unit power gain" (custom simulator; p. 6 takes the LoS probability from [49]); the paper never uses 3GPP TR 38.811 or 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "Increasing the number of subcarriers grows the NSCs until it reaches K = 16" is a sweep of K, U, DTh and number of UAVs; the paper never states that a trained policy is tested on an unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 12: "MARDPG achieves higher performance than MADDPG, DSAC, and Greedy"; p. 15: "MARDPG roughly has a 6% gap compared to the exhaustive search" (NSCs metric).
q4_support: p. 10: "the CC of MARDPG is CCMARDPG" with order O((E x Hbatch x HLSTM) x CCneural x B) in Table 1; p. 15: "its running time is dramatically high (80 times higher than MARDPG)" (Table 4: 12 ms versus 960 ms).
q5_support: p. 12: "all the source codes related to this paper can be found in [76]"; p. 18: reference [76] is a dataset on IEEE DataPort with DOI "10.21227/xsb6-ah82".
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Included: the learned MARDPG chooses uplink power and subcarrier allocation of aerial links jointly with UAV location and CPU cycles, so it passes above_phy (p. 8); area 6 by function. Channel is a custom Rayleigh and air-to-ground simulator, not a 3GPP model. Tables 1-5 were read as images (pp. 10, 11, 14, 15, 16).
